summary.intent: Design a production-ready rollout plan for a memory loop system, starting from a PoC that demonstrated the concept but used throwaway architecture (JSON storage, broken outcome tracking). The goal was a clean-slate spec with incremental PR-sized delivery path.
summary.outcome: A comprehensive design spec was written at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md` with 8 vertical-slice PRs, multiple mermaid diagrams, open architecture questions for code owners, and enriched scoring design informed by the agent-memory reference project. The spec treats all PoC code as throwaway.

repo: The PoC memory loop tasks 1-3 (state model, reconciliation, mode/policy) are production-quality with passing tests and should not be discarded; only the storage backend and outcome tracking need replacing

The PoC's DeriveOutcomes at memoryloop.go:1091-1138 uses bag-of-words overlap (overlap > 0 at line 1120) — a single shared programming term marks a memory ineffective, making outcome tracking actively harmful
The PoC stored memories as a JSON file which won't scale for concurrent access or querying
insightsdb uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS without a versioned migration strategy, which is a pattern to avoid in the rewrite
EntireDB exists as a potential remote sync target for repo-scope memory sharing

code.finding: DeriveOutcomes uses bag-of-words token overlap. Any single shared token (including common programming words like 'test', 'run', 'error') between memory text and post-injection session text marks the memory ineffective. The claimed '3+ injection cycles' safeguard checks InjectCount > 0, not >= 3 — the safeguard does not exist.
Outcome flip condition is `overlap > 0` — single token match causes incorrect ineffective verdict
Uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS without versioned migration — schema evolution requires ALTER TABLE additions; no migration framework in place

workflow: Adversarial review is valuable for design docs, not just code — it surfaced fundamental broken assumptions (outcome tracking, leading questions, straw-man comparisons) that a standard review would miss

When designing a multi-PR rollout, vertical slices (each PR delivers one working end-to-end feature) are preferable to horizontal layers (storage → model → injection → ...) because each PR is demoable
Referencing similar open-source projects during design phase yields concrete scoring algorithm improvements that would otherwise require months of iteration
For clean-slate rewrites, explicitly stating 'no migrations, no backwards compatibility' in the spec prevents scope creep and over-engineering early PRs

friction: Codex adversarial review companion script (codex-companion.mjs) crashed with ENOBUFS on every attempt because the worktree had 32 untracked files causing git spawnSync buffer overflow — the script cannot target a specific file, it always diffs the full working tree
Multiple API 500 errors from Anthropic at session end blocked the user from getting an explanation of structured memory fields
The Codex review had to be replaced with a self-review agent, which worked but added latency and broke the intended tooling flow

The first version of the spec needed substantial rework after adversarial review (migration handling, straw-man Option C comparison, broken outcome tracking, made-up size estimates) — the initial design passed through without catching these issues
open_items: Code owners need to decide storage architecture: Option A (SQLite local only for beta) vs Option B (SQLite + checkpoint git branch) vs Option C (SQLite + EntireDB) for repo memory sharing in Phase 2
Auto-refresh trigger mechanism is unresolved: after N sessions, on commit hook, on session end, or time-based — listed as Q15 in spec with no recommendation
Embedding-based semantic similarity scoring deferred to Phase 2/3 — schema should include nullable embedding column so memories don't need regeneration when added
Outcome tracking redesign (signal-based, not bag-of-words) is specified but disabled for Phase 1 — needs implementation validation before enabling
Repo memory sharing design (Phase 2) depends on code owner storage decision — sync protocol, conflict resolution, and manifest format are hand-waved in the spec
Hard questions about schema migration failure handling, concurrent write contention, and beta telemetry mechanism are listed as open questions (Q24-Q27) without answers

Multi-signal scoring (file overlap + semantic + error signature + recency + importance with quality gate) from agent-memory project not yet incorporated into spec — identified as high-value but needs spec update
